labels.note: The source (page 2, section 9-2 Cooking, rule c) states: 'The water shall be vaporized in a single container and the starting water weight shall be at least 96.00 oz (2.721 kg).' The extracted value 96.00 oz, unit, quote, and lower-bound meaning are correct. However, the claim assigns it to 'Contest 9-3 Dinner Party' and lists region 'table' with basis 'unknown', when it is actually a textual requirement in 9-2 Cooking, so scope/condition and basis are wrong.

The source is Table 5-1, titled 'Drivetrain Properties', with a caption stating it summarizes drivetrain properties discussed in the section. The table lists rotor/generator speeds, gearbox ratio, generator efficiency, inertia, driveshaft spring/damping constants, and brake torque/time constant. The 'about' statement correctly identifies it as a summary of these drivetrain properties and lists the included categories without giving specific numerical values or design choices.

The middle panel (FFA-W3-211, 77% span) shows the pressure side contains carbon/UD near LE, medium-density foam, and glass_triax mainly as outer/skin layers, plus gelcoat near TE. So glass_triax is present but is not the sole material composition there. The entity, span, quote, and chart kind match the source.

A shows the grade-level datum (0") in a Harvest deck-footing detail (S-522), while B gives a bedroom finished-floor height (2'-9 1/2" relative to grade) in a Borealis building-section drawing (A-303). The source images show different company logos and unrelated sheet/section numbers, indicating competing proposals rather than corresponding parts of one design, so pairing them is not sensible and they are not complementary.

Figure 9 shows the scoring line flat at 0 points up to 16 oz, then rising linearly to full points at 80 oz, with the right-hand box listing 'Reduced points: 16 oz (450 g)' and 'No points: Weight ≤ 16 oz'. The x-axis ticks include 20, but the linear increase starts at 16 oz, not 20 oz. The quoted axis label does not establish a 20 oz start point.

A shows the NREL 5-MW baseline controller pitch angle of 23.47° at 25 m/s with rotor speed 12.1 rpm. B describes the IEA 15-MW blade-pitch controller objective to regulate speed to 7.55 rpm over 10.59–25 m/s. These are different turbine designs with different rated speeds, so they are not the same entity or corresponding parts of one system.

Table 4-1 on page 12 lists 'Young's modulus, steel' with symbol E and value '2 00E11' in units Pa, i.e., 2.00E11 Pa, matching standard steel modulus. The quote and value align with the highlighted row, and no conditions or qualifiers are omitted.

The source (Figure 2-6, blade cross section at 70% span / Section 0.7) shows a material stack legend that includes Medium Density Foam, Glass Triax, Glass Biax, Carbon UD, Glass Uni, and Gelcoat. Thus Carbon UD is present in section 0.7, but it is only one of several materials, not the entire composition.

Image 1 shows the title-block section labeled 'STRUCTURAL ENGINEER' with 'ARUP ENGINEERING' and the address '1120 CONNECTICUT AVENUE, NW., SUITE 200 WASHINGTON, DC 20036'. Image 2 is page 4 with 'S-901 FRAMING ISOMETRICS' and a red-boxed title block on the right where this information resides. The extracted address matches the source exactly and is correctly tied to the structural engineer entry.
The highlighted text on page 12 states the resulting gains include K_I(θ = 0°) = 0.008068634, matching the quoted value, entity, condition, and kind. No misread or misbinding is present.

Figure 10 shows the scoring line reaching exactly 100 points at 0 kWh net electrical energy, and the table lists 'Full points: Net electrical energy ≥ 0 kWh', so 100 points at 0 kWh is correct. However, the value is exact on the chart/definition, not approximate, and the quoted text stitches axis labels and a point rather than quoting a single source sentence.

Figure 10 shows the Energy Balance Contest scoring curve relating net electrical energy to points, with linear reduced points between -50 and 0 kWh and full/no points outside that range. The description correctly identifies the graph and its purpose, but the role explicitly cites the -50 kWh and 0 kWh boundaries, which are specific values shown in the figure.

Figure 9 in section 9-2 Cooking shows the scoring box with 'No points: Weight ≤ 16 oz (450 g)' for vaporized water, matching the value, unit, and quote. However, the claim attaches this rule to 'Contest 9-3' (Dinner Party) instead of the Cooking subcontest (9-2), so the scope/condition is wrong.

Image 1 (detail E6) shows the roof beam opening with dimensions 2'-1", 8", 6", and 2". The 2" dimension is placed at the lower side of the opening, corresponding to bottom clearance/offset, while 6" is the opening height; it is not the offset from the top edge. The entity, quote, unit, and detail reference are otherwise correct.

The drawing page (A-202) lists West Elevation (A1) with left-side elevation markers: SOLAR ENVELOPE, FINISHED FLOOR, and GRADE LEVEL. The FINISHED FLOOR line is near 2 ft, but the visible annotation reads closer to 2'-0" (possibly 2'-0 1/2"), not 2'-3". The extractor kept only the foot portion (2 ft) and misquoted the inch part.

The sheet A-301 is titled BUILDING SECTIONS and contains two labeled section drawings: C1 SECTION - WEST MODULE and A1 SECTION - EAST MODULE. Both show vertical cuts through the buildings with marked FINISHED FLOOR and GRADE LEVEL lines, matching the description of East/West module sections including those levels. No specific dimensions or design choices are stated.

Page 3 shows drawing callouts C1 (Module B structural member) and the S-701 PV DETAILS table at bottom right. The claim assigns C1 a thickness of 3/16 in., which matches the table context and notation; no contradictory value is visible, though the table cells are small and not fully legible in the crop.
